Independent structural review rejected comm_apology_0004: Evidence fails: “jurors” is not established by the printed passage or cited records. Placement passes: edge follows “vehement slanders” and precedes “From among them Meletus...”.

Independent structural review rejected comm_apology_0007: The synthesis is accurate and listenable, but the edge follows “desert my post...” and precedes “It would be a terrible thing...,” displacing the 28b anchor into 29a.

Independent structural review rejected comm_apology_0009: The title’s “Arginusae” identification lacks matching printed or accepted support; the body is otherwise anchored and concise. Before: private-life conclusion; after: promised deeds.

Independent structural review rejected comm_apology_0014: The opening misreads Socrates: he rejects choosing known evils over Meletus’s uncertain penalty, rather than refusing any harm he regards as known evil. Placement and listening pass.

Independent structural review rejected comm_apology_0018: Evidence and listening pass, but playback snaps +931: it follows the sons’ rebuke and precedes “If you do this,” so the recap arrives after most of its span.

Independent structural review rejected comm_apology_0022: Evidence and listening pass, but the edge falls before 19a: after the prior accusers’ charges and before “Well, then…19a,” displacing commentary anchored at 19b–19c.

Independent structural review rejected comm_apology_0025: The claims are supported, but this is bare recap of the politician episode and overlaps the section's summary; before is the oracle-wide investigation, after begins its results.

Independent structural review rejected comm_apology_0050: The argument is supported, but the edge follows the prytaneum exchange and precedes its proposed penalty, displacing commentary on exile into the wrong exchange.

Independent sample review rejected comm_charmides_0010: Its summary substantially overlaps the two additional blocks at the identical playback edge, creating a redundant three-block interruption before the dream argument.

Independent structural review rejected comm_charmides_0012: The summary is accurate and useful, but playback follows “if you actually have it” and precedes “See now whether you have it,” after the anchored close.

Independent structural review rejected comm_charmides_0013: Accurate, but it repeats the section's return, setting, Critias, and topic-shift recap. At the edge, nothing precedes it and the same opening source follows.

Independent sample review rejected comm_charmides_0038: Although accurate alone, it duplicates the adjacent section and notice at the same playback edge, so the stacked interruption is unnecessarily repetitive.

Independent sample review rejected comm_charmides_0039: Its accurate dream-and-happiness analysis overlaps the section and neighboring argument at the same edge, producing an overpacked redundant interruption.

Independent structural review rejected comm_charmides_0044: The argument is accurate and focused, but playback follows the prior health exchange and precedes “For health, we said,” before its 175b–175e anchor.

Independent structural review rejected comm_crito_0002: The dream and Crito’s appeals are supported, but “the text leaves its meaning at that level” asserts an unsupported absence; the edge falls after “Too clear” before “But, my dear Socrates.”

Independent structural review rejected comm_crito_0013: Accurate and well placed between Crito's agreement and Socrates' next question, but it substantially repeats the section's trainer-to-justice explanation and should be differentiated.

Independent structural review rejected comm_euthydemus_0016: The critic's disparagement and reported-speech frame are supported, but the passage does not establish that philosophy becomes a public target; rewrite that overreach.

Independent structural review rejected comm_euthyphro_0002: Fails placement: immediately before is Socrates asking “Whom?” and immediately after is Euthyphro’s answer; this splits a question from its answer.

Independent sample review rejected comm_euthyphro_0020: The body says Euthyphro has already said the gods quarrel, but before this edge he has only confirmed the definition; Socrates raises divine quarrels next, making the temporal attribution premature.

Independent structural review rejected comm_gorgias_0032: Evidence and listening pass; placement fails: before the edge Call asks, “you are the man...?”, and after it Socrates begins, “Apparently I can,” splitting question from answer.

Independent structural review rejected comm_greater-hippias_0002: The synthesis is clear and well placed after Socrates’ setup and before Hippias’ reply, but “lost his inheritance” exceeds the source’s claim that money was left to and lost by Anaxagoras.

Independent sample review rejected comm_greater-hippias_0006: The playback edge falls between Socrates’ request to teach him and Hippias’s immediate reply, splitting a direct prompt and response; this requires prompt_reply_split and interrupts_dramatic_flow.

Independent sample review rejected comm_greater-hippias_0007: The playback edge follows Socrates’ question, “Then are not all beautiful things beautiful by the beautiful?”, and precedes Hippias’s immediate answer, creating a question_answer_split hazard.

Independent sample review rejected comm_greater-hippias_0009: The playback edge follows Socrates’ question asking what the beautiful is and precedes Hippias’s immediate definition, creating a question_answer_split hazard.

Independent structural review rejected comm_laches_0002: The title calls Laches and Nicias generals without packet support; the body mostly recaps, narrows Socrates’ setting, and overstates his deferral as disclaiming knowledge.

Independent structural review rejected comm_laches_0004: Accurately frames Laches’ skepticism and examples, but the edge follows the preceding question and precedes Lach.’s immediate answer, splitting question from reply.

Independent structural review rejected comm_laches_0009: The summary is accurate and clear, but the edge follows Laches’ question, “What do you mean?”, and precedes Socrates’ immediate answer, splitting question from reply.

Independent structural review rejected comm_laws_0034: “After scrutiny” reverses the source’s sequence: the priest is tested after receiving the lot. The edge follows Clin.’s reply and precedes Ath.’s new sentence, so placement is safe.

Independent structural review rejected comm_laws_0035: Evidence and listening pass, but the edge follows the choir proposal and precedes Ath.'s direct reply; snapping +1268 chars displaces the hinge into the music-official exchange.

Independent structural review rejected comm_laws_0046: Evidence and listening pass, but the edge follows a semicolon after the obedience claim and precedes “Ath. a more complete statement,” splitting the continuing clause.

Independent structural review rejected comm_laws_0054: Evidence supports the catalogue, demand, and prelude; “must address beliefs” is too certain. Placement passes: prior text ends “loosed...”; next begins “Ath. Next...”

Independent structural review rejected comm_laws_0066: Evidence and spoken focus pass, but playback follows the time-limit sentence and precedes Ath.'s forceful-obstruction rule, displacing the section opening into a later exchange.

Independent structural review rejected comm_lesser-hippias_0006: Evidence and listening pass. Placement splits Socrates’ accusation, “You are deceiving me,” from Hippias’s immediate reply, “Not at all.”

Independent structural review rejected comm_lysis_0005: Accurate, concise overview, but remove: the edge falls after Lysis says they stop many things and before Socrates asks “How do you mean?”, splitting prompt and reply.

Independent structural review rejected comm_lysis_0007: Evidence and listening pass, but playback follows “so fond I am of my comrades.” and precedes “Accordingly, when I see you and Lysis together,” shifting this section into 212a.

Independent structural review rejected comm_menexenus_0009: Evidence and listening pass, but the edge follows the 242e conquest sentence and precedes Socrates’ third-war account, displacing commentary on the later 243d-e reversal.

Independent structural review rejected comm_menexenus_0013: Evidence and listening pass, but playback snaps +1071 chars: before is the proverb's close; after is Socrates beginning a later self-reliance exposition, displacing the section.
Independent structural review rejected comm_meno_0002: The recap is useful and accurately tracks the exchange, but “every bearer” broadens Socrates’ male/female comparisons beyond the cited evidence.

Independent structural review rejected comm_meno_0011: It states as settled that the soul acquired the opinions earlier and is immortal, flattening Socrates’ conditional inference; it follows “Twice” and precedes 85b’s geometry.

Independent structural review rejected comm_meno_0014: Evidence is accurate and concise; the edge falls between Socrates’ question “is it by education?” before and Meno’s immediate answer after, splitting Q/A.

Independent structural review rejected comm_meno_0016: The body accurately frames the later inference, but the edge follows Socrates’ claim that virtue is not teachable and precedes Anytus’ rebuke, displacing the unit’s dramatic setup.

Independent structural review rejected comm_meno_0018: The closing claim that “nothing will be clear” overstates the source’s narrower condition: certainty about how virtue comes requires first defining virtue.

Independent structural review rejected comm_parmenides_0005: Evidence and listening pass. Playback shifts +1476 chars: before is the shape conclusion at 138a; after begins Ceph.'s exposition that the One cannot be anywhere, displacing the 137c anchor.

Independent structural review rejected comm_parmenides_0006: Playback falls after 140e: before is the completed age exchange; after is Ceph's 141a time question. This displaces the 140a section overview into a later topic.

Independent structural review rejected comm_parmenides_0010: The commentary is supported and clear, but the edge follows the One's being/existence exchange and precedes its generation discussion, before the later turn to the Others.
